en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kāsumāraphaliya Kaṇikāra Chapter 3 I am a bhikkhu who has attained the goal; having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the final state. Having exhausted the taints, I dwell in peace. This is my last body. In the past, when the lifespan was twenty thousand years, there appeared in the world the Blessed One Kassapa, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He was endowed with wisdom and conduct, the Sugata, the one who understood the worlds, the unsurpassed guide for those needing training, the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. At that time, I was a householder in Benares. I went to the monastery and saw the Tathāgata. Having seen him, I took a kāsūmāra fruit and offered it to the Blessed One. Because of that root of merit, I was reborn in heaven. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I experienced the fruits of that deed. Now, having passed away from there, I have been reborn here in this human world. I have become a bhikkhu who has attained the goal; having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the final state. Having exhausted the taints, I dwell in peace. This is my last body. This is the account of the Elder Kāsumāraphaliya. It is finished.
“I saw the stainless Buddha sitting amidst the mountains, shining like a *kaṇikāra* flower.”
To the Eldest in the World, the Bull among Men—
with a clear mind and a joyful heart,
placing his joined palms upon his head—
I gave it to the Best of Buddhas.
The fruit that I gave back then—
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
The defilements have been burnt away by me; ... [as before] ...
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Kāsumāraphaliya spoke these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Kāsumāraphaliya.
